deep.reconstruction:
Authorship and context. This page is not a research note by Riemann. It is an editor's draft of the endnotes ('Anmerkungen') to Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Ueber die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe', which is Abhandlung XII of the Gesammelte Werke (1876, edited by Weber with Dedekind). Three things show this. The heading reads 'Zu der Abhandlung XII ... mit kleinerem Satz', a typesetting instruction to print in smaller type. The paragraph references are left blank ('Zu §. ...'), awaiting page numbers. The continuation on the next page cites Genocchi, Turin 1875, after Riemann's death.

Note (1). Setting from Riemann's text: f has period 2π. F(x) = C + C'x + A0 x^2/2 - Σ A_n/n^2. By Satz I, the quotient Δ(α,β)F(x)/(4αβ) tends to f(x), where Δ(α,β)F(x) = F(x+α+β) - F(x+α-β) - F(x-α+β) + F(x-α-β). By Satz II-III, n^2 ∫_b^c F(x) cos n(x-a) λ(x) dx tends to 0 for admissible λ: λ and λ' vanish at b and c, and λ'' is piecewise monotone.

The editor supplements Satz II in the following steps.

(i) Put φ(x) = F(x+2π) - F(x). Since f(x+2π) = f(x), Δ(α,β)φ(x)/(4αβ) → 0 as α, β → 0.

(ii) Hence φ is linear, φ(x) = p + qx. [My gloss: this needs φ continuous, which holds because F is continuous. It also needs the Schwarz lemma: a continuous function whose second symmetric derivative is identically 0 is linear (Schwarz, around 1870-72). The note does not state this justification.]

(iii) Choose constants so that Φ(x) = F(x) - C'x - A0 x^2/2 has period 2π. Indeed Φ(x+2π) - Φ(x) = p + qx - 2πC' - 2πA0 x - 2π^2 A0. So take A0 = q/(2π) and C' = (p - 2π^2 A0)/(2π).

(iv) Subtracting a quadratic preserves the limit property. Since ∫ x^k cos μ(x-a) λ dx = O(μ^-2) after two integrations by parts, μ^2 ∫_b^c Φ(x) cos μ(x-a) λ(x) dx → 0 as well.

(v) Take b < -π and c > π, with λ = 1 on [-π, π]. Split the integral over [b, c] into the pieces [b, -π], [π, c] and [-π, π].

(vi) For μ = n an integer, both Φ(x) and cos n(x-a) have period 2π. Substituting ξ = x + 2π moves the piece over [b, -π] onto [b+2π, π], with weight λ(ξ - 2π). The two outer pieces then combine to n^2 ∫_{b+2π}^c Φ(x) cos n(x-a) λ1(x) dx. Here λ1(x) = λ(x-2π) on [b+2π, π] and λ1(x) = λ(x) on [π, c]. λ1 is again admissible on [b+2π, c], since both parts equal 1 with zero derivative at x = π.

(vii) By the hypothesis, that combined term tends to 0. Therefore n^2 ∫_{-π}^{π} Φ(x) cos n(x-a) dx → 0. In other words, n^2 times the Fourier coefficients of the periodic part Φ tends to 0.

The margin jottings (x = ξ + 2π, ξ = x + 2π, Φ(x - 2π), Φ(ξ) cos μ(ξ-a) λ(ξ-2π)) are the editor's working of this substitution.

Note (2), begun here. For Riemann's later proposition, the editor says λ should additionally be assumed 2π-periodic. This is compatible with the earlier assumptions. The next page gives a counterexample without periodicity and sketches a proof with it.
errors: The text says λ1(x) = λ(x + 2π) on [b+2π, π]. The substitution ξ = x + 2π actually gives λ1(ξ) = λ(ξ - 2π). The margin computation 'λ(ξ - 2π)' is correct; the main text has a sign slip.
The first combined integral is written with cos μ(x-a), but μ has already been specialised to the integer n. This is a notational slip only.

The step 'second symmetric difference of φ tends to 0, hence φ is linear' is asserted without justification. It requires continuity of φ plus the Schwarz lemma (or Riemann's own Satz-type argument). It is true, but the note leaves it implicit.
The note silently assumes that λ is smooth across ±π, so that λ1 meets the regularity conditions at x = π. This is harmless, since λ = 1 with λ' = 0 there.
Margin line 'ξ = x + 2π' sits alongside 'x = ξ + 2π'. These are inconsistent scratch notes; the correct relation, consistent with λ(ξ - 2π), is ξ = x + 2π.

results.what: A function whose generalized second symmetric difference quotient tends to 0 is linear. Hence the integrated series F differs from a 2π-periodic function by C'x + A0 x^2/2.
results.modern_name: Schwarz's lemma (vanishing Schwarz/Riemann second symmetric derivative implies linearity)
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (c. 1870-72), used by Cantor in the uniqueness theorem

results.what: Reducing μ^2 ∫_b^c Φ cos μ(x-a) λ dx → 0 to n^2 ∫_{-π}^{π} Φ cos n(x-a) dx → 0 by periodic shifting of the localizing factor λ.
results.modern_name: Riemann localization / Riemann's third lemma; vanishing of n^2 × Fourier coefficients
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Habilitationsschrift 1854, publ. 1867); this editorial supplement is by the Werke editors (Weber/Dedekind, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an editorial endnote for the 1876 Gesammelte Werke edition of Riemann's Abhandlung XII. It carries a typesetting instruction, blank paragraph references, and on the next page a citation of Genocchi 1875, all after Riemann's death. It is therefore not Riemann's own work, and its content is a routine gap-filling argument.

checkable.asserts: The second symmetric difference of cos is 4 sin(α) sin(β) cos(x). This is the identity on the previous page and should simplify to 0.
A linear φ has zero second symmetric difference; should give 0.
With these constants, Φ = F - C'x - A0 x^2/2 satisfies Φ(x+2π) - Φ(x) = 0 when F(x+2π) - F(x) = p + qx; should give 0.
cos n(x-a) has period 2π for integer n, which justifies the shift of the integration interval; should give 0.

transcription_corrections: The phrase 'um 2π' is inserted above the line, between 'eine' and 'periodische Function', and is not in the main line as transcribed. The intended reading is '... eine um 2π periodische Function von x ist'.
The last phrase before 'Null' is uncertain. 'für Null' is probably a misreading of 'gleich Null' or similar; the intended sense is 'the limit ... is zero'.
The margin reads 'Φ(ξ) cos μ(ξ-a) λ(ξ-2π)'. The transcription renders this as 'Φξ cos μ(ξ-a) λ(ξ-2π)'; the content is the same, with Φ(ξ) meant.
'Riemann 8' at top right is an archival label, not part of the text.
